usage.callShape: POST https://stableupload.dev/api/upload with JSON body {filename, contentType, tier}. Returns a presigned S3 upload form; you then upload the actual file bytes to S3 in a separate request.
usage.outputShape: body.publicUrl (permanent download URL once file is uploaded). Upload mechanics: body.uploadMethod ("post"|"put"), body.postUrl + body.postFields (S3 multipart fields) for POST, or body.uploadUrl for PUT. body.curlExample is a ready-to-run upload command. body.uploadId, body.expiresAt, body.maxSize, body.uploadUrlExpiresAt also returned.
quirks: TWO-STEP FLOW: this endpoint does NOT accept file bytes. POST /api/upload only ISSUES a presigned S3 form; you must perform a SECOND request to actually upload the file. For uploadMethod=='post', POST the file to body.postUrl as multipart/form-data including every key/value in body.postFields PLUS a 'file' field with the bytes (body.curlExample shows the exact fields). For uploadMethod=='put', PUT the bytes to body.uploadUrl.

PRICE IS TIER-DEPENDENT, not flat $2. Registry $2 surface = '1gb' tier. Cheaper tiers: 10mb=$0.02, 100mb=$0.20, short-10mb=$0.005, short-100mb=$0.02, short-1gb=$0.10, short-5gb=$0.50. 'tier' is required; pick the smallest that fits your file to minimize cost. (Tested with short-10mb = $0.005.)
Presigned upload form expires quickly (uploadUrlExpiresAt ~15 min); upload the file promptly. publicUrl/download expires at body.expiresAt (7 days for short-* tiers, 6 months for default tiers).
publicUrl returns the file only AFTER the second-step S3 upload succeeds; it 404s before that.
txHash field in the response was null on this call.
usage.guide: Call POST https://stableupload.dev/api/upload with JSON {filename, contentType, tier} where tier is the smallest that fits the file (e.g. short-10mb for <10MB, ~$0.005). The response is a presigned S3 upload ticket, NOT a confirmation that the file is stored. Second step: actually upload the bytes — if uploadMethod is "post", send a multipart/form-data POST to postUrl including all postFields plus a "file" part (body.curlExample is the exact command); if "put", PUT the bytes to uploadUrl. After that succeeds, the file is permanently downloadable at body.publicUrl until body.expiresAt. No auth/API key required; payment is per call via x402.
